clue.text: Game bird is hot when swallowed by a hick

indicators.note: being swallowed means going down inside the second word, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a hick is a country bumpkin, a peasant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A yokel gobbles a hot game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a common game bird shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Lifting short raincoats is a crafty trick

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the word upward, so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: macs, short for mackintoshes, are raincoats

explanation.surface: Someone pulls up a raincoat as part of a sly ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' belongs with the raincoats: MAC is the shortened form of mackintosh, so it is not a deletion signal. 'Lifting' turns MACS upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a swindle, a dishonest crafty trick to cheat someone.

clue.text: Searched for "The King and I" and then took flight

parts.note: R, for Rex, is the abbreviation for king
fled means ran away, took flight

explanation.surface: Someone hunted for the musical The King and I and then ran off.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search hastily through something, often to steal.

clue.text: This cow in marshy land preserves the right

indicators.note: to preserve something is to hold it safely within, so the marsh word encloses the other

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cow standing in a marsh keeps hold of its right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning to intimidate.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate or scare them into submission.

clue.text: Moving round Spain with gusto, feeling faint

indicators.note: letters moving round each other end up in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone touring Spain enthusiastically starts to feel dizzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Passing out means fainting, losing consciousness, which follows feeling faint.

clue.text: Small horses take one sip without restraint

indicators.note: letters free of restraint run loose and fall into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rider lets small horses drink freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Ponies are horses of a small breed, under about fourteen hands high.

clue.text: Very large woman's jacket of a kind

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for woman
a hacking jacket is a tweed riding jacket with slanted pockets

explanation.surface: A lady's jacket comes in an enormous size.
explanation.walkthrough: A hacking jacket is a British tweed riding jacket; 'of a kind' says only the qualifying word is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Whacking is informal British slang for very large, as in a whacking great bill.

clue.text: Food's past, showing a wash is needed

parts.note: grub is slang for food
by means past, as in walking by

explanation.surface: Food has gone off, and the dishes plainly need washing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grubby is dirty, grimy, and so in need of a wash.

clue.text: "About A Boy" ought to be kept in mind

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as in business letters
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: The title About A Boy is worth remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted film title is just three wordplay pieces; 'ought to be kept in' is linking padding before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Reason is the power of sound thought, the mind, as in losing one's reason.

clue.text: Friend having married, sure sign of a winner

parts.note: a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend getting wed is the surest token of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A palm branch was the ancient emblem of victory, hence bearing the palm.

clue.text: Loaf getting flatter, not for formal dinner

parts.note: to loaf is to idle or lounge about
to suit someone is to flatter their looks, as a colour suits you

explanation.surface: Bread being squashed flat is no use at a dinner party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' and 'flatter' read as bread and a comparative adjective, but both are verbs.
explanation.definitionFit: A lounge suit is ordinary business wear, worn when evening dress is not required.

clue.text: Like Harlequin, pray when in the sea

indicators.note: one word placed in another means it sits inside it

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
to pray is to ask or beg

explanation.surface: A harlequin-like figure says prayers out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Harlequin of the commedia dell'arte traditionally wears a black mask.

clue.text: White-skinned,red-mottled, he at last succeeded

definitions.meaning: describes a British potato variety with pale skin splashed with red
the long-waiting Prince of Wales who finally followed Victoria on the throne in 1901

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to both a well-known potato variety and the British monarch who reigned 1901 to 1910.

clue.text: Plant expert born near station curiously

indicators.note: done curiously, the letters come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A horticulturist was born near a station, oddly enough.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanist is a scientist who studies plants.

clue.text: Play with pots and kettles to repair

definitions.meaning: to fiddle or meddle with something idly
describes the travelling mender of pots and kettles

explanation.definitionFit: Tinker is both a verb meaning to fiddle with and a noun for an itinerant mender of metal pots.

clue.text: Let years unhappy bring to mind a blow

indicators.note: letters that are unhappy are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Sad years let go make one recall a cruel shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a blow' looks like a misfortune, but it means a wind; 'bring to mind' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind from the east, and a blow is a gust or gale.

clue.text: I'm wearing nothing, having an affair

parts.note: in means wearing, as in a woman in red
love means nothing, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to being naked while having a fling.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'I'm wearing nothing' as 'I'm in love': 'I'm' just frames it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in love describes an amorous attachment, as in a romance or affair.

clue.text: Extend the angle badly formed with toe

indicators.note: letters badly formed are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.surface: Lengthen the corner that is misshapen with a toe.
explanation.definitionFit: To elongate is to lengthen, to extend something further.

clue.text: Rose, half-cut, fills opening, being smart

indicators.note: one piece filling another goes inside it

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal opening into a mine

indicators.note: cut in half, only the front part of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A slightly tipsy woman called Rose fills a doorway, looking sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' suggests drunk, but it takes RO from Rose; ADIT is a mine entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means clever or skilful, quick-witted, which is one sense of smart.

clue.text: Left to keep rent when let out of the nick

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: red describes the political left
to lease is to rent

explanation.surface: A tenant still owes rent when freed from prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the nick' is British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To be released from the nick is to be freed from prison.

clue.text: Nice little job for student who can't start

indicators.note: a word that cannot start loses its opening letter

parts.note: a learner is a student

explanation.surface: A good little job for a student unable to begin work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a nice little earner' is a British phrase for a profitable sideline.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is a job or scheme that brings in money.

clue.text: A poet's dream increased by half a tick

annotationWithheld.why: A poet's dream increased by half a tick (6): MOON (dream) with TI (half of tick) inside gives MOTION, but no clue word is left to define MOTION; the definition appears to be missing or doubling as wordplay.
annotationWithheld.clue: A poet's dream increased by half a tick

clue.text: I can't believe it when my bottom shows!

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of disbelief or scorn
the bottom of one's leg, the lowest part of the body

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of disbelief and, literally, the bodily extremity at one's base.

clue.text: Downhearted little brother kept away

parts.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother
owned means possessed, kept
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: A depressed little boy has been sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: Browned off is British slang for fed up, disheartened.

clue.text: To chat about a Forsyte novel, say

indicators.note: turned about, the word reads backwards

parts.note: to gas is to chat idly

explanation.surface: Discussing a Galsworthy novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forsyte Saga is Galsworthy's novel sequence, an example of a long family saga.

clue.text: Who helps make sausages? This person knows

definitions.meaning: describes a herb used to flavour sausages

explanation.definitionFit: Sage is both a herb used in sausage seasoning and a wise person.

clue.text: They say the bird's a shade of blue

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the petrel is a seabird

explanation.surface: A bird's feathers are reportedly a certain blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrol blue is a deep greenish blue, so petrol names that shade.

clue.text: Yet good man backed these points of view

parts.note: though means yet, however

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: St, for saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Yet a virtuous man supported these opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: Thoughts are opinions or ideas, one's points of view.
